title: Datadog for Claude Cowork. Observability by conversation.
decision: Pilot the Datadog connector with one team, keep Datadog permissions scoped, and treat the Preview status as a rollout risk.
summary: The Datadog plugin and connector let Claude query Datadog logs, metrics, traces, dashboards and monitors through the Datadog MCP Server.

claims.text: The Datadog MCP Server bridges Datadog observability data to AI agents, so logs, metrics, traces, dashboards and monitors can be queried in natural language.
For Claude, including Claude Cowork, the official Datadog connector is the recommended path and includes MCP Apps for in-product visualizations.
Claude Code installs the Datadog plugin from the official Anthropic Plugin Marketplace; the plugin bundles the MCP Server with skills and auto-updates.
Setup asks you to choose a Datadog site and sign in with OAuth in the browser; API and application keys are a supported alternative.
Remove any separately registered Datadog MCP server or custom connector first to avoid conflicts.
You need Datadog permissions for the resources you query, and the plugin states that no Datadog credentials are sent to the AI model provider.
Groups of MCP tools can be enabled or disabled with the toolsets command.
The Datadog plugin and its marketplace listing are in Preview.
The Datadog MCP Server is HIPAA-eligible, customers remain responsible for the compliance of the AI tools they connect, and the server is not supported on the Datadog government sites.

sections.title: A bridge. Not a dashboard.
sections.body: The Datadog MCP Server links your observability data to any agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol, so you ask instead of clicking through screens.

voice.narration:
Datadog for Claude Cowork. Your telemetry, one question away. Here is what the plugin does, how it connects, and where a team should be careful.

The Datadog Model Context Protocol server bridges your observability data to agents. Logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, and monitors become things you can simply ask about.

For Claude, including Cowork, the official connector is the recommended path, and it adds in-product visualizations. Claude Code installs the same server as a plugin from the official marketplace.

Setup is short. Choose your Datadog site, then sign in with O Auth in the browser. Keys are an alternative, and any older manual server or custom connector should be removed first.

Access is not widened. You still need the Datadog permissions for the data you query, and the plugin states that no Datadog credentials are sent to the model provider.

Tool groups can be switched on or off, so a team can expose only the products it needs. Start with one narrow toolset.

Treat the preview label as a rollout risk. The server is H I P A A eligible, yet you own compliance for the tools you connect, and government sites are not supported. Pilot with one team, keep permissions tight, then expand.
